question: How many ordered pairs \((a,b)\) such that \(a\) is a positive real number and \(b\) is an integer between \(2\) and \(200,\) inclusive, satisfy the equation \((\log_b a)^{2017}=\log_b(a^{2017})?\)
solution:
The logarithm power rule turns the right side into \(2017\log_b a\), so it is useful to set \(u=\log_b a\). The equation becomes
\[
u^{2017}=2017u,
\]
or
\[
u\bigl(u^{2016}-2017\bigr)=0.
\]
Thus
\[
u=0\quad\text{or}\quad u=\pm\sqrt[2016]{2017}.
\]
The two nonzero values arise because 2016 is even.

Write \(r=\sqrt[2016]{2017}>0\). For each fixed allowed base \(b\), converting back through \(a=b^u\) gives exactly three solutions:
\[
a=1,\qquad a=b^r,\qquad a=b^{-r}.
\]
All are positive and distinct, since \(b^{-r}<1<b^r\).

There are \(200-2+1=199\) possible bases. Each gives three pairs, and different bases give different ordered pairs because their second coordinates differ. Therefore the total is
\[
199\cdot3=\boxed{597}.
\]
The answer is E.
